context:
Core execution-variant guardrails (added 2026-10-09; ADR docs/development/adr/adr-core-execution-variants.md, plan item core-exec-execution-variants):
- Do not register bare generic option keys (engine, mode, backend, runtime, executor, warehouse); the vocabulary parity test fails on them.
- Deployment is declared through the manifest deployment_modes capability and selected with --platform aiven-clickhouse:<mode>.
- The Aiven service is a named compute resource: use the core compute_resource/compute_size per core-exec-compute-resource-unification, with vendor spellings as aliases. If that item has not landed, stop and ask whether to wait or add a native key that will become an alias.
- Follow the execution-variant section of docs/development/new-platform-acceptance-checklist.md.
description:
Add the Aiven for ClickHouse native platform adapter, modeled on ch-altinity-adapter (AivenAdapter(ClickHouseAdapter), key `aiven-clickhouse`, experimental). Aiven publishes literal connection recipes for both native (clickhouse-driver, secure=True) and HTTPS transports.

DECISION GATE: proceeds only after ch-tier2-spike records a go for Aiven AND wave 1 (Altinity adapter) has landed, so shared hosted-ClickHouse patterns are visible before cloning. If the Altinity adapter reveals abstraction-worthy duplication, propose the shared base in that PR rather than here.

Guardrails: same as Altinity adapter (manifest authority, lazy imports, compat-docs-check, no credentials, 7-10 files).
